title: kv-cache: improve memory accounting, adaptive eviction and spillover compaction
author: Priya Kapoor
description: Context: We continue to see production tail latency and OOM pressure on high-concurrency workloads caused by KV cache fragmentation, suboptimal spillover/paging decisions, and lack of global memory accounting across shards. This PR consolidates prior heuristics (v36..v40) and introduces three coordinated changes: 1) stricter per-shard and global memory accounting with 'resident' vs 'spillable' classifications, 2) an adaptive eviction scheduler that shifts between LRU, age-priority, and size-aware compaction modes based on fragmentation metrics, and 3) background spillover compaction + on-demand paging thresholds that reduce cross-device page thrashing. The change is gated behind a runtime flag and a canary rollout. Key motivations: reduce end-to-end token-latency variance, avoid OOMs when many small prompts create fragmented KV state, and lower memory amplification on mixed-length workloads. This PR includes benchmarks, diagnostics, and rollout steps. Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked (Linear ENG-12987, ENG-14002) - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] Microbenchmarks (latency and throughput) - [x] Canary config and runtime flag - [x] Back-compat: defaults off for Dedicated until canary completes Related: previously merged work on defrag scheduler (PRs v31..v40), adaptive compaction experiments (ENG-14002).

4) Tests: add kv_cache_memory_manager_test and perf harness scenarios
5) Docs: add runtime flags and rollout notes to ops/kv-cache.md

release_notes: Improved KV cache memory accounting and adaptive eviction scheduler to reduce fragmentation and spillover-induced latency spikes. Includes background compactor and new observability metrics. Default disabled for Dedicated; opt-in via runtime flag for canary.
benchmarks_summary: Microbenchmarks (local perf harness): tail 99p latency down 18-28% on mixed-length workloads; average throughput unchanged (+/- 2%); memory amplification reduced by 25% in fragmentation-heavy scenario; canary in prod (5% traffic) showed reduced OOM rate and stable latencies after 24h.
rollout_and_risks: Default: feature flag = off; Canary: enable for 5% of traffic in two dedicated pools for 48h; Monitoring: fragmentation_ratio, spill_rate, compaction_time, and OOM count. Rollback: disable flag, compactor gracefully drains. Risks: aggressive compaction can temporarily increase GPU memory pressure; mitigations included backoff heuristics and circuit-breaker when compaction increases spill_rate.
ops_instructions: ops/kv-cache.md contains runtime flags: kvcache.enable_adaptive_eviction, kvcache.compaction_budget_mb, kvcache.paging_threshold_percent. Canary steps, dashboard panels, and alert thresholds included.
notes: This consolidates many prior incremental patches into a single coordinated behavior change; per earlier discussion we keep default off for Dedicated until full canary completes and SRE sign-off is obtained.
audits_and_metrics_changes: Added metrics: kvcache.fragmentation_ratio, kvcache.spill_rate, kvcache.compaction_duration_seconds, kvcache.resident_bytes_total. Dashboard panels updated in ops/kv-cache.md.
testing_notes: Unit tests cover accounting and scheduler mode transitions. Integration test simulates multi-tenant mixed-length workload and asserts no OOM and acceptable latency SLOs. Perf harness used to generate numbers in benchmarks_summary.
changelog_entry: kv-cache: adaptive eviction + spillover compaction (opt-in canary).
backwards_compatibility: Config-gated and default off; no API changes; internal storage layout unchanged. Migration: none required.
notes_for_release_manager: Flag must be explicitly enabled in Dedicated clusters. Ensure alerts for increased compaction_duration and spill_rate are set before progressive rollout.
